symptom: `make test` failed on main right after #1670 (git doctor) merged, in a hosted sandbox only: TestGitDoctor_SSHRemoteRewrittenByFix and TestGitDoctor_SSHURLFormRewrittenByFix reported `remote url = "https://github.com/org/app.git\n", want https://github.com/org/app`; CI was green
cause: `git remote get-url` applies url.<base>.insteadOf, and the tests ran git under the developer's own configuration. The sandbox sets GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE rewriting git@github.com: and ssh://git@github.com/ to https://github.com/, so the SSH remote the test added already read back as HTTPS and --fix never touched it; a ~/.gitconfig rewriting https://github.com/ to git@github.com: (the usual developer setup) fails the same two tests the other way, `git@github.com:org/app`
insight: A test that shells out to git inherits three configuration sources besides the repository's — system, global, and the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT environment — and isolating HOME or the identity variables covers none of the third. Reproduce each source separately, because they fail in opposite directions: env rewrite on this host, then `env -u GIT_CONFIG_* HOME=<dir with an https->git@ insteadOf>`, with an empty HOME as the passing control. Both failed before the fix and pass after. Not fixed, and a product question rather than a test one: with a global https->git@ rewrite, `git doctor` reads the effective URL, so it reports SSH and `--fix` sets an HTTPS URL that the rewrite turns straight back into SSH, every run
